original_question: If G⃗ is a Borel locally finite directed graph whose indegrees are uniformly bounded and whose out-neighborhoods have polynomial growth, is the connected equivalence relation of G⃗ hyperfinite?
target_in_paper: Section 13, Problem 44 (Wei Dai): "If G is a Borel locally finite directed graph whose in-degrees are uniformly bounded and out-neighborhoods have polynomial growth, is the connected equivalence relation of G hyperfinite?" This is the exact paper statement your draft is aiming at. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s official formulation. It correctly identifies the object as a Borel locally finite directed graph, includes the uniform bound on in-degrees and the polynomial-growth assumption on out-neighborhoods, and asks exactly whether the connected equivalence relation is hyperfinite. In substance, it is Problem 44 with only cosmetic notation changes. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, the ambient vertex set should be named explicitly as a standard Borel space X, with the directed edge relation G⃗ viewed as a Borel subset of X × X. Problem 44 states this only tersely through the phrase "Borel locally finite directed graph." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))

The phrase "connected equivalence relation of G⃗" should be unpacked explicitly as the equivalence relation E_G⃗ on X where x E_G⃗ y iff x and y lie in the same connected component of the underlying undirected graph obtained by symmetrizing G⃗. The paper does not restate this convention inside Problem 44. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))

The growth condition should be quantified in a self-contained rewrite: for example, there exist constants C and d such that every forward n-ball B_n^+(x) has size at most C n^d for all x and all n, or equivalently the forward balls are bounded by a fixed polynomial. Problem 44 uses only the shorter phrase "out-neighborhoods have polynomial growth." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))

A stand-alone version should spell out that hyperfiniteness is meant in the standard countable-Borel-equivalence-relation sense: E_G⃗ is an increasing union of finite Borel equivalence relations. Problem 44 asks about hyperfiniteness but does not reintroduce the definition there. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))

No extra hypotheses should be added. In particular, the nearby discussion mentions broader hyperfiniteness questions for group actions and for graphs of uniform subexponential growth, but Problem 44 itself is the narrower directed-graph question with bounded in-degree and polynomial forward growth. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
refined_question: Let X be a standard Borel space, and let G⃗ be a Borel locally finite directed graph on X. Assume that there is a uniform bound M < infinity such that every vertex has in-degree at most M, and that the forward balls have polynomial growth, in the sense that there exist constants C, d < infinity such that for every x in X and every n in N, the set B_n^+(x) of vertices reachable from x by a directed path of length at most n has cardinality at most C n^d. If E_G⃗ is the equivalence relation on X of belonging to the same connected component of the symmetrization of G⃗, must E_G⃗ be hyperfinite? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
justification: The exact target is Section 13, Problem 44, which your draft essentially reproduces verbatim. The nearby hyperfiniteness context in Section 11 explains the intended scope: the paper first recalls known positive results for orbit equivalence relations of several amenable-type groups and for connected equivalence relations of graphs of polynomial growth, then asks about graphs of uniform subexponential growth. Against that backdrop, Problem 44 is best read as a tightly focused directed-graph analogue, not as a broader question about all subexponential-growth graphs or all amenable equivalence relations. The rewrite therefore stays narrow and only makes the standard hidden conventions explicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2507.03972))
